proposals.before: Book of Sui, 44th year of Volume, ninth year of Biographies
proposals.after: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine
proposals.reason: Chinese 卷四十四列傳第九 means Volume 44, Biographies 9, not regnal or ordinal 'years'.

proposals.before: Prince Teng the Mu, Zan, styled Hengsheng and also known as Hui, was a maternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
proposals.after: Prince Teng the Mu, Zan, styled Hengsheng and also known as Hui, was a younger brother of Emperor Gaozu by the same mother.
proposals.reason: 母弟 means younger brother of the same mother, not maternal cousin; later 異母弟 for Shuang confirms siblingship.

proposals.before: Teng the Mu Prince Zan, styled Hengsheng, also named Hui, was a younger cousin on Empress Gao's side.
proposals.after: Teng the Mu Prince Zan, styled Hengsheng, also named Hui, was Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother.
proposals.reason: 高祖母弟 is Gaozu's same-mother younger brother, not a cousin of Empress Gao.

proposals.before: After Gaozu took the throne, Song was posthumously created Prince of Dao with the temple name Xuan.
proposals.after: After Gaozu took the throne, Song was posthumously created Prince of Dao with the posthumous name Xuan.
proposals.reason: 諡曰宣 is a posthumous name (諡), not a temple name (廟號).

proposals.before: After Gaozu took the throne, Zheng was posthumously created Prince of Cai with the temple name Jing.
proposals.after: After Gaozu took the throne, Zheng was posthumously created Prince of Cai with the posthumous name Jing.
proposals.reason: 諡曰景 is a posthumous name (諡), not a temple name (廟號).

decisions.reason: 卷四十四列傳第九 is Volume Forty-Four, Biographies Nine; the idiomatic line wrongly reads 卷/第 as 'year' and invents regnal-style dating that the Chinese does not support.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 隋書卷四十四列傳第九

decisions.reason: 高祖母弟 means Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother, not a maternal cousin; the proposed idiomatic wording restores the kinship correctly.
高祖母弟 is Gaozu's same-mother younger brother; the literal wrongly takes 高祖 as Empress Gao and 母弟 as cousin on her side.
諡曰宣 grants the posthumous name Xuan (諡), not a temple name (廟號); replacing 'temple name' with 'posthumous name' matches the Chinese.
諡曰景 grants the posthumous name Jing (諡), not a temple name (廟號); the proposed replacement is accurate.
